content: TTC8, also referred to as Bardet-Biedl syndrome 8, is a protein in humans encoded by the TTC8 gene. TTC8 is functionally associated with gamma-tubulin, BBS4, and PCM1 within the centrosome. PCM1, in turn, plays a critical role in centriole replication during the process of ciliogenesis. TTC8 is specifically localized in the cilia of spermatids, retinal cells, and bronchial epithelial cells. Mutations in the TTC8 gene are one of the 14 identified genetic causes of Bardet-Biedl syndrome.
